answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments form an information-theoretic anchor, rendering identity cloning computationally infeasible by demanding an intractable expenditure of sequential work for forging consistent reputation chains. Each ZK-STARK proof, validated via verifiable delay functions, forms an unforgeable attestation. An attempt to spoof an identity would need to echo the legitimate computational history, incurring an astronomical, verifiable cost and thus establishing an oasis of secure, attributable agency.
